issue.title: Critical RCE in Playwright-MCP Server via browser_run_code

comments.body: See https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp?tab=readme-ov-file#security. Also please follow https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md for reporting security issues.

comments.body:
I previously submitted a report for this issue, but it was rejected.

For reference, I shared my analysis and PoC here:

It seems to me that this issue is describing the same underlying vulnerability.

Best wish!

comments.author: TianYu-0829

comments.body:
The useful design lesson here is that browser automation tools probably need action-scoped permissions, not just one broad “can run code / can’t run code” switch.

Reading an accessibility tree, evaluating page state, clicking, typing into a draft field, uploading a file, and pressing Submit are different risk classes. They should be exposed as separate capabilities with separate approval gates.

For agent workflows, I’d rather see the default path look like:

- inspect page / accessibility tree freely
- draft proposed browser actions
- require approval before external side effects
- leave an activity artifact showing what was observed, changed, refused, and why

That doesn’t settle the sandboxing question in this issue. But it does make the agent boundary much easier for users to understand and audit, especially when indirect prompt injection is part of the threat model.
